key_insight: The paper turns Gaussian entanglement quantification into a convex-geometric optimization problem, yielding efficiently computable upper bounds on entanglement and two-way-assisted quantum/private communication for multimode optical systems.
engineering_relevance: These bounds provide practical performance limits for lossy/noisy photonic links, helping engineers assess when entanglement distribution, teleportation, or key distribution can be resource-feasible under energy constraints.
method: Derive integral/geometric formulations for Gaussian-restricted relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement.
Exploit positive-partial-transpose Gaussian reference states and matrix geometric means to obtain unique optimizers and additivity for independent inputs.
Use a convex-majorization algorithm with controlled numerical integration and approximate subproblem solves to achieve polynomial bit-complexity for fixed rational covariance matrices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit convergence and bit-complexity guarantees, plus two- and three-mode numerical examples that compare the bounds against achievable rates and recover pure-loss benchmarks.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees apply to Gaussian-restricted quantities and fixed rational covariance inputs; extending to unrestricted, large-scale multimode systems still requires photon-number truncation and careful error control.
paper_title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
